title: Exploration of common pathogenesis and candidate hub genes between HIV and monkeypox co-infection using bioinformatics and machine learning.
authors: Li, Jialu; Hao, Yiwei; Wu, Liang; Liang, Hongyuan; Ni, Liang; Wang, Fang; Wang, Sa; Duan, Yujiao; Xu, Qiuhua; Xiao, Jinjing; Yang, Di; Gao, Guiju; Ding, Yi; Gao, Chengyu; Xiao, Jiang; Zhao, Hongxin
one_liner_zh: 该研究用生物信息学和机器学习分析HIV与猴痘共感染的差异基因和枢纽基因，虽涉及转录因子网络，但核心是疾病共病机制而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，且无AI/物理模拟方法用于结合机制研究。
abstract: This study explored the pathogenesis of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and monkeypox co-infection, identifying candidate hub genes and potential drugs using bioinformatics and machine learning. Datasets for HIV (GSE 37250) and monkeypox (GSE 24125) were obtained from the GEO database. Common differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in co-infection were identified by intersecting DEGs from monkeypox datasets with genes from key HIV modules screened using Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA). After gene ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis and construction of protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, candidate hub genes were further screened based on machine learning algorithms. Transcriptional factors (TFs) and miRNA-candidate hub gene networks were constructed to understand regulatory mechanisms and protein-drug interactions to identify potential therapeutic drugs. Seven candidate hub genes-MX2, ADAR, POLR2H, RPL5, IFI16, IFIT2, and RPS5-were identified. TFs and miRNAs associated with these hub genes, playing a key role in regulating viral infection and inflammation due to the activation of antiviral innate immunity, were also identified through network analysis. Potential therapeutic drugs were screened based on these hub genes: AZT, a nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor, suppressed viral replication in HIV and monkeypox co-infection, while mefloquine inhibited inflammation due to the activation of antiviral innate immunity. In conclusion, the study identified candidate hub genes, their transcriptional regulation, signaling pathways, and small-molecule drugs in HIV and monkeypox co-infection, contributing to understanding the pathogenesis of HIV and monkeypox co-infection and informing precise therapeutic strategies.
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了人类免疫缺陷病毒（HIV）与猴痘合并感染的发病机制，利用生物信息学和机器学习方法识别候选枢纽基因及潜在药物。从GEO数据库获取了HIV（GSE 37250）和猴痘（GSE 24125）的数据集。通过将猴痘数据集中的差异表达基因（DEGs）与使用加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）筛选出的关键HIV模块中的基因取交集，识别出合并感染中的共同差异表达基因。在基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）富集分析以及蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络构建后，基于机器学习算法进一步筛选候选枢纽基因。构建了转录因子（TFs）和miRNA-候选枢纽基因网络，以理解调控机制和蛋白质-药物相互作用，从而识别潜在治疗药物。鉴定出七个候选枢纽基因：MX2、ADAR、POLR2H、RPL5、IFI16、IFIT2和RPS5。通过网络分析，还识别出与这些枢纽基因相关的转录因子和miRNA，它们在抗病毒先天免疫激活中发挥关键作用，调控病毒感染和炎症。基于这些枢纽基因筛选出潜在治疗药物：AZT，一种核苷逆转录酶抑制剂，抑制HIV和猴痘合并感染中的病毒复制，而甲氟喹则抑制由抗病毒先天免疫激活引起的炎症。总之，本研究识别了HIV和猴痘合并感染中的候选枢纽基因、其转录调控、信号通路及小分子药物，有助于理解HIV和猴痘合并感染的发病机制，并为精准治疗策略提供依据。
